note: Nigeria, read on the Nigeria Immigration Service's own pages (the visa classes and the Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Aliens Card, CERPAC, both read 2026-10-30; neither is dated). A performer coming for an event has the Creative Arts Visa, up to 30 days (the work engine's route). To live and work in Nigeria a foreigner hired under an approved Expatriate Quota comes on the Employment (Expatriate) Visa, enters for 90 days and is then granted a residence and work permit, typically for two years and renewable, allowing formal employment for the employer only (read as work for the sponsor). The CERPAC that carries it costs USD 2,000 for employed foreigners, USD 600 for students and nothing for foreigners married to Nigerian citizens; fees here are in US dollars as the Service sets them. The Permanent Residence Visas include the Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa (employment under the sponsoring arrangement) and the Spouse of Nigerian Citizens Visa (employment may be allowed if properly authorised, read as work for a sponsor); the page does not say which CERPAC fee the highly skilled pay, so none is kept. No term is stated for the permanent visas. ECOWAS citizens' right of residence, naturalisation's years and decision times were not on these pages and were not read elsewhere.

sources.title: Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Aliens Card (CERPAC), Nigeria Immigration Service (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: The essence of CERPAC is to allow foreigners live and work legally in Nigeria for an extended period, usually One (1) year and above, subject to renewal. ... Pay the applicable fees online (USD 2,000 for employed foreigners, USD 600 for Students and Gratis for foreigners married to Nigeria citizens) ... Spouse of Nigerian Citizens Visa ... Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa

sources.title: Nigerian Visa, Nigeria Immigration Service (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: Temporary Residence Visas allow individuals reside in Nigeria for a period not exceeding two years (2 years), subject to renewal, for the purpose of employment ... Used by foreign nationals hired under an approved Expatriate Quota. Valid for an initial 90-day entry, then a residence/work permit is typically granted for two years (renewable). ... The visa allows formal employment but excludes unauthorized outside work. ... Permanent Residence Visas permit certain class of individuals to obtain permanent residence status in Nigeria. ... Employment is permitted under the sponsoring arrangement, subject to compliance with local labor and immigration rules. ... Employment may be allowed if properly authorized, though terms vary by regulation.
